searchText: What version of Node and npm are used in `execution-apis` ? I'd be happy to set a minimum for the repo's `package.json` That way moving forward, everyone that joins will at least have the same exact dependency tree in `node_modules` when they `npm install`. Prevents issues like "well, it worked on my local environment..." 😂 Also, I'm looking at ``` "params": [ { "name": "Proof-of-work hash", "required": true, "schema": { "$ref": "#/components/schemas/bytes32" } }, ``` ... how would I change this to an 8 byte type ? I can't find `byte8` base type here: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/schemas/base-types.json Actually I figured it out.. The base-types.json was throwing me off. ``` "byte": { "title": "hex encoded byte", "type": "string", "pattern": "^0x([0-9,a-f,A-F]?){1,2}$" }, "bytes": { "title": "hex encoded bytes", "type": "string", "pattern": "^0x[0-9a-f]*$" }, ???? <----------------------- I was expecting a bytes8 with a title like "8 hex encoded bytes" or a pattern like "pattern": "^0x[0-9a-f]{16}$" "bytes32": { "title": "32 hex encoded bytes", "type": "string", "pattern": "^0x[0-9a-f]{64}$" }, ``` Is this right? https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/124 i think lts (v14.15.1) would be a good min i think you're gonna need to create the type since it hasn't been used before Would that be necessary? I found another "Nonce" type elsewhere and it was using the regular `bytes` schema. https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/schemas/block.json#L82-L85 bytes allows an arbitrary number of bytes, we should use the most prescriptive types that we can in the spec and in the case of the PoW nonce (different than account nonce) the max size is only 8 bytes so is `src/schemas/base-types.json` the proper place to define bytes8 ? yes it is! should I define bytes16 while i'm at it? is there such a thing? And do these data types come from solidity data types? a quick internet scan says that bytes1, bytes2, bytes3,... up to bytes32.... exist in Solidity. I guess for now, i'll just define bytes8 and if a new one comes around, just define that then. i would keep the diff minimal, only added what is necessary at this time I just noticed something. Does it matter that the pattern for `byte` allows for characters `[0-9,a-f,A-F]` but the patterns for `bytes`, `bytes32` `bytes64` are only lowercase `a-f` ? this could be something we look into more, but generally i wrote this to be as strict as possible and so AFAIK geth doesn't return any uppercase hex values (maybe a checksum address? but don't recall) i think it accept upper case hex, but for the spec i think it's better to say it's not accepted to maintain strictness no worries. I'll just go wth the least amount of changes and continue the consistency with the other bytes types thank you - be sure to be mindful of this existing issue https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/issues/106 actually sorry - i don't think this is an issue with bytes8 because it *must* be 8 bytes, `0x0` is invalid is that issue just fixing the pattern to allow 0x0? i think so okay i fixed that too. I'll be updating the PR in a min cool. It's ready for review. I kept the two issues as two separate commits. LMK if you want me to squash that into 1 commit. https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/124
